intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honour all of them. Today's roll was seed 3187176492. Here's each roll and what came of it. Did you HEAR about it? You're about to.

rolls.became: Mona is a monstera, root-bound in a pot two sizes too small in flat 3B of Marrow Court, and anxious about it the way only a cramped plant can be. Marrow Court is above Auntie Ko's ramen shop, and for forty years the landlord has packed its walls with the shop's leftover tangles instead of plaster. Every strand Mona untangles leaves a gap a root can grow into.
Hold the knot of noodles poking out behind her pot and Mona's root takes up the strain; let go when the ring is full and a strand pops loose. Later, the same hold is how she leans in to eavesdrop.
Room for her roots. The comfort meter is how much of the building her roots have reached: root-bound, fidgety, settling, spreading out, roomy, sprawling, comfy.
Mr. Pettibone, who wrote Clause 14 (no plants) himself, has salted the walls of the roof, his office and the basement "against damp". Roots won't go near salt.
Mona, Marrow Court, and the thing in the basement every noodle loops back to: the Mother Knot.

rolls.value: a map you explore and reveal
rolls.became: The building, cut away like a doll's house, every room a wall of solid noodle until a root breaks through. Roots feed on the loose strands, so noodles are what you spend to reach a room and to fill it with roots.

rolls.value: a second, parallel game that opens midway
rolls.became: With roots in six tenants' flats, the walls stop being muffled: roots carry every word. The Party Wall opens beside the knot, a second little game about holding on just long enough. The juicier the gossip, the more dirt. And dirt on Pettibone is exactly what gets his salt swept out.
Every rooted room boosts its four neighbours. The bath's forty-year drip waters the roots next door, the hot pipes warm them, the light well brightens them, and a full room boosts twice as hard.
About two hours across a sitting or two. The roots keep untangling while you're away, slowly.
Noodles into the quintillions. Dirt stays in the hundreds and thousands: gossip is precious.
Everything is cut like a two-block print: a plum key block, rose and mauve tint blocks, peach paper, and the noodles carved as loops gouged through the dark.
Four colours, and a woodcut needs no more: plum, mauve, dusty rose and peach.

Pettibone's Invention: a fussy two-part harpsichord invention in the Japanese in-sen scale (D E-flat G A C), for the ramen shop downstairs. When the grapevine opens, a second voice copies the tune a bar late, the way gossip gets passed along. Every sound effect is on the same five notes.
Did you HEAR? Two kettles in 2A. The landing DIPS. Pettibone eats at Ko's for free. Everyone in Marrow Court talks, and Mona hears all of it.

rolls.value: a holiday or festival near the release date
rolls.became: Japan's Culture Day falls on 3 November, when schools hold their culture festivals. Pim in 3C is building a noodle sculpture for theirs, and everyone in the building is going.

The gossip kept circling the dipping landing and the basement nobody's allowed in, and Pettibone's diary page said it outright: the knot is holding EVERYTHING up. On festival afternoon, with the building empty, Mona pulls it. Marrow Court folds down like a soufflé into one soft heap of noodles, and a garden.

rolls.value: an epilogue that keeps playing itself as the credits roll
rolls.became: The tenants come home to tables in the garden, Auntie Ko ladles ramen from the heap, Pettibone sweeps up his salt, and Mona, planted in real ground at last, keeps untangling all by herself while the credits roll round and round.

outro: None of this was planned. The dice said houseplant, noodles, landlord, harpsichord. Everything else is just what happens when you take that seriously.
